error.signature: AI tells someone that artisanal raw-milk cheese in Brazil legally requires 60 days of aging before sale, or that any artisanal cheese can now be sold nationwide without certification

verdict.summary: Brazil's old blanket rule requiring 60 days of minimum aging (maturação) for raw-milk artisanal cheese was superseded by Lei 13.860/2019 and Decreto 11.099/2022, which created the Selo ARTE (Artisanal) national seal: cheeses aged under 60 days can be produced and sold legally, but only from facilities in a traditionally recognized cheesemaking region using herds certified free of (or under control for) tuberculosis and brucellosis, and only once the product carries the ARTE seal or a state-equivalent seal - informally made or uncertified raw-milk cheese under 60 days old remains restricted.

dead_ends.action: State that Brazilian law flatly requires 60 days of aging before any raw-milk cheese can be legally sold
dead_ends.why_fails: This was the rule under older federal sanitary regulations, but Lei 13.860/2019 and its regulating Decreto 11.099/2022 removed the blanket 60-day minimum: cheeses aged under 60 days are legal to sell when made in a facility located in a certified or traditionally recognized cheesemaking region, from herds free of (or under control for) tuberculosis and brucellosis under Brazil's national brucellosis/tuberculosis control program (PNCEBT).
dead_ends.common_misconception: The 60-day rule was widely cited for over a decade (including by cheesemakers themselves) and is still repeated as current law in many summaries, even though the underlying decree it was based on was revoked in 2022.

dead_ends.action: Assume any artisanal raw-milk cheese bought from a farm or informal producer can now be legally resold or shipped to another state because '60-day aging is no longer required'
dead_ends.why_fails: The relaxed maturation rule only applies to producers who hold the Selo ARTE (or an equivalent state seal) and operate in a certified/traditional cheesemaking region with disease-free herds; informal producers without that certification, or without SIM/SIF registration for the relevant sales channel, are still restricted in where they can legally sell, and uncertified raw-milk cheese under 60 days old sold outside those channels remains a food-safety and regulatory violation.
dead_ends.condition: Producer or seller does not hold the ARTE seal or equivalent state certification

workarounds.action: Look for the Selo ARTE (or a state-equivalent artisanal seal) on the cheese label before assuming under-60-day raw-milk cheese is safe to buy and legal to transport across state lines
workarounds.how: The ARTE seal indicates the producer's herd is certified free of tuberculosis and brucellosis and the product followed the traceability and safety requirements set under Decreto 11.099/2022, allowing nationwide commercialization.

workarounds.action: When advising a producer, point them to their state's agricultural defense agency (e.g. IMA in Minas Gerais) to confirm current regional requirements, since the ARTE seal is administered at the state level
